newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: HAVAS CZECH UNIT SIGNS RADIO AD SALE DEAL.
newsitem.headline: HAVAS CZECH UNIT SIGNS RADIO AD SALE DEAL.

text.p: The Czech unit of the French communications group Havas, IP Praha, said on Thursday it had signed an exclusive contract for advertising sales for the Czech public radio Cesky Rozhlas (CRo).
IP said it would start selling 1997 advertising time for CRo in November in an exclusive deal to the year 2000.
"The yearly turnover of (CRo's) advertising is roughly 100 million crowns," IP Praha's Regina Sehnalova told Reuters.
Cesky Rozhlas broadcasts on four nation-wide and eight regional stations, and advertising on public radio is limited to 0.2 percent of the total broadcasting time.
The Czech advertising market has grown quickly in recent years as many foreign companies have launched their brands.
IP expects advertisers to spend a total of 10.65 billion on Czech media buying this year, after 9.39 billion in 1995.

"The market will rise, but not so much as in the past years," IP Praha marketing director Rene Jaz said. "There were many campaigns bringing in new brands, which are very costly. Now there are more campaigns to maintain (brand image)."
He said press advertising had 43 percent of the market, followed by television with 37 percent, while radio advertising takes around seven percent of the total spending.
